record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space X such that every bounded linear operator A in L(X) attains its norm, meaning that for each A there is some unit vector x with ||Ax|| = ||A||?

evidence.quote: We say that A ∈ L(X) attains its norm if there exists x ∈ X such that ||x|| = 1 and ||Ax|| = ||A||.
Problem 12.1. Does there exist an infinite dimensional Banach space X such that each A ∈ L(X) attains its norm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a Banach space and let L(X) denote the Banach algebra of all bounded linear operators A : X → X equipped with the operator norm ‖A‖ = sup{‖Ax‖ : x ∈ X, ‖x‖ = 1}. An operator A ∈ L(X) is said to attain its norm if there exists x ∈ X with ‖x‖ = 1 such that ‖Ax‖ = ‖A‖.

Question: Does there exist an infinite-dimensional Banach space X (over the real or complex field) with the property that every A ∈ L(X) attains its norm?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open for real or complex Banach spaces. Recent surveys on norm-attaining operators (e.g., M. Martín, 2024) and related literature still list it as an unresolved question. A construction is known only in non-standard settings (e.g., over the field GF(2)), which does not address the classical case.

status_evidence.title: An overview on norm attaining linear operators (M. Martín)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of norm-attaining operator problems including the question of whether every operator on some infinite-dimensional Banach space attains its norm.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented as an unresolved question in a 2024 survey on norm-attaining operators.

status_evidence.title: Properties of an infinite dimensional Banach space over the field with two elements
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of an infinite-dimensional Banach space over GF(2) on which every bounded linear operator attains its norm.
status_evidence.claim: A non-standard analogue is established over GF(2), but the real/complex case remains open.
